case_name: Charles Lin and Amy Lin v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Retired; standard deduction elected; rented basement room to friend for ten months at $300/month.

adjustments: unreported Social Security benefits $32,808, 85% taxable: adjustment $27,887
unreported retirement income: adjustment $11,344 (other retirement income $61,973 treated as 100% taxable)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Taxable amount of railroad retirement (Social Security) benefits; increased Schedule E loss claimed on amended return

findings_of_fact.fact: Original return: dividends $4,010, taxable Social Security zero, retirement benefits $61,976 of which $50,629 taxable
findings_of_fact.snippet: they reported (as relevant here) dividends of $4,010, taxable Social Security benefits of zero

findings_of_fact.fact: Rented a room to a friend for ten months at $300/month, total rent $3,000; no written lease
findings_of_fact.snippet: a modest rent of $300 per month , yielding total rental income of $3,000.

findings_of_fact.fact: Original Schedule E loss $8,189 allowed by IRS; expenses insurance $604 and taxes $10,430 for whole house (and Florida timeshare)
findings_of_fact.snippet: On their 2019 return petitioners reported on Schedule E a rental real estate loss of $8,189.

findings_of_fact.fact: No evidence of square footage of tenant space or its percentage of house
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioners supplied no evidence concerning the square footage of the space occupied by the tenant

findings_of_fact.fact: Amended return claimed Schedule E loss of $30,763 with additional expenses totaling $22,729
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioners claimed on their amended return a Sched- ule E loss of $30,763, as compared with the loss of $8,189 they had orig- inally reported.

findings_of_fact.fact: Repairs ($3,913) incurred to renovate basement bathroom only after tenant moved out
findings_of_fact.snippet: incurred in connection with renovation of their basement bathroom but only after the tenant

findings_of_fact.fact: Received railroad retirement benefits treated as Social Security benefits totaling $32,808
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioners concede that they received during 2019 r ailroad re- tirement benefits totaling $32,808.
For 2019 petitioners had modified AGI of $53,456—adjusted gross income of $53,174 as reported on their original return, plus $282 of omit- ted dividend income.

findings_of_fact.fact: MAGI + half of benefits = $69,860; base amount (joint) $32,000; excess $37,860
findings_of_fact.snippet: Adding to that sum one-half of their Social Secu- rity benefits, or $16,404, yields $69,860.
Adding the lesser amount, or $6,000, to $21,981 yields $27,981 of taxable Social Security benefits.
For peti- tioners that amount is $27,887 ($32,808 × 0.85).

issues.question: Other (Schedule E rental loss, §§162/212/469(i)): are petitioners entitled to the additional $22,729 of rental expenses (Schedule E loss of $30,763 vs $8,189 originally reported) claimed on their amended return?
issues.holding: Not entitled: no evidence to allocate whole-house expenses to rented space; HOA fee unrelated; repairs incurred after tenant left; $8,189 original loss left undisturbed
issues.computable_reason: Substantiation/allocation failure of proof; no evidentiary basis for estimate.

issues.question: What portion of petitioners' $32,808 of railroad retirement (Social Security) benefits is taxable for 2019?
issues.holding: $27,887 taxable (85% cap), as determined in the notice
issues.computable_reason: Pure §86 formula from MAGI $53,456, benefits $32,808, joint base amounts.

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Taxable SS benefits $27,887 sustained; dividends $282 conceded; retirement income adjustment conceded by IRS; no additional Schedule E loss.

notes: Opinion cites the 85% cap as §86(b)(2)(B) (statute: §86(a)(2)); also says 'calculated under section 86(b)(1)(A)' for $27,981. Original Schedule E mis-summed expenses ($11,034 vs $11,189; $155 error). No penalty determined. Stipulated facts incorporated.
